elements.name: API handlers
elements.description: Validate input, extract bearer key; bound query/execute to 2.9 seconds.

elements.name: Route client + cache
elements.description: Caches grants for 60 seconds; refresh after 10 seconds; evicts stale epochs.

elements.name: Control circuit breaker
elements.description: Stops failing control calls; usage report bypasses this breaker.

elements.name: Node client + row stream
elements.description: 2.5 second attempts; transcodes row streams; tolerant response reader.

elements.name: Read retry policy
elements.description: Jitter, two retries, deadline and token budget; never retries uncertain writes.

elements.name: Request shedding + HTTP boundary
elements.description: 24 concurrent requests by default; noncritical share 6 slots; health/metrics bypass; logs.

elements.name: Admission + SQL engine
elements.description: Epoch check, per-database lanes, tenant/node limits; 2 second statement deadline.

elements.name: Handle manager
elements.description: Bounded pools and LRU; singleflight open; close releases resources.

elements.name: Backup job + blob client
elements.description: Snapshots under writer lock; uploads after releasing lock.

elements.name: Bounded usage queue + shippers
elements.description: 1024 queued events; four shippers; batches up to 100; overflow after 20 ms.

elements.name: Outbox access + sweeper
elements.description: Reads at most 500 rows every 5 seconds; deletes only after delivery.

elements.name: Maintenance + drain
elements.description: Checkpoints WALs; evicts idle handles; SIGTERM stops admission and spills usage.

documents.title: Litefleet: system context explained
documents.plain: Litefleet gives tenants named SQLite databases. A tenant application sends a bearer API key and SQL. The operator reads fleet usage and runs the lab. Backups go to a blob-store partner; usage batches go to a metering partner. Both partners are Go fakes in this Compose lab. This describes the hardened code, not a production service. Open Litefleet to see its containers. Each database has one owning node; there is no replication, move protocol or automatic failover.

ste.text: The tenant sends SQL to Litefleet. The operator reads usage. Litefleet sends backups and usage to two test partners. Each database stays on one node. Open Litefleet to see the containers.

documents.title: Litefleet: containers explained
documents.plain: HAProxy balances three gateways. Each gateway uses cached routes or asks control to authenticate the key and locate the owning node. Gateway-to-control and gateway-to-node traffic uses Toxiproxy in the lab. Control sends provision/drop commands directly to nodes; nodes send heartbeats directly to control every 5 seconds. Heartbeats populate the Postgres usage ledger independently of partner metering. Control uses distinct 8/2/1-connection OLTP/report/health pools. Each of two node agents owns tenant SQLite files and a separate _node.db outbox. Replicas are collapsed in this view; the deployment view names them. Open Gateway or Node agent for components.

ste.text: HAProxy sends each request to a gateway. The gateway finds the owning node. Control keeps routes in Postgres. Each node keeps tenant files and an outbox on its own volume. Open a gateway or node for more detail.

documents.title: Litefleet: gateway components explained
documents.plain: All six responsibilities run in each gateway process. All requests except health and metrics pass through a 24-request shed limit; noncritical routes share 6 slots. Query and execute share a 2.9 second request deadline. The route cache serves entries for 60 seconds, refreshes after 10 seconds, and evicts stale epochs. Remote resolve uses the control breaker and bounded read retries; the usage-report client bypasses the breaker. The node client gets 2.5 seconds per attempt, retries reads only before a response begins, and streams rows by decoding and re-encoding them. It never repeats an uncertain write. A stale_epoch refusal can trigger re-resolve and resubmission because no SQL ran. A draining response is passed back with Retry-After, without retry. Streaming errors after headers abort the answer rather than report false success.

ste.text: These components run in one gateway process. The gateway limits load and request time. It can use a saved route. It retries some reads before the answer starts. It does not retry a write with an unknown result. A partial stream is an error.

documents.title: Litefleet: node components explained
documents.plain: All six responsibilities run inside each node process. Admission checks epochs and limits work to two reads and one writer per database, four statements per tenant and sixteen per node. The engine uses a 2 second statement deadline and 250 ms pool wait. Queries stream with a 1000-row / approximately 1 MiB JSON cap and a truncated flag. Statements return connections on every path; the handle LRU has 128 entries and idle eviction. Backup takes a snapshot under a writer lock and uploads after releasing it. The usage queue has 1024 slots; overflow after 20 ms and failed sends go to usage_outbox in _node.db. The sweeper redelivers stored rows. Maintenance checkpoints WALs above 64 KiB or after idle time. SIGTERM rejects new work, waits for admitted work, closes handles and spills queued/stuck events. These measures do not make arbitrary crashes or disk failures lossless.

ste.text: Each node owns its database files. It limits concurrent statements and statement time. It releases the backup lock before upload. The queue stores overflow on disk. On a normal stop, the node saves pending usage. A crash can still lose events in memory.

documents.title: Litefleet: bounded query flow explained
documents.plain: The steps show a successful read with a conditional cache-miss lookup. A valid route cache hit skips steps 3–5; an older live entry may also start a background refresh. Reverse steps are replies on the same relationship, not additional API calls. Query/execute get 2.9 seconds overall, node attempts 2.5 seconds and node statements 2 seconds. Overload is refused with 429/503 and timeouts before streaming can return 504; failures after stream start cut the connection. Reads may retry transient failures only before answer start and within retry/deadline budgets. No uncertain write retry is shown. A stale_epoch refusal permits one re-resolve; draining is returned to the tenant.

ste.text: The gateway can use a saved route. Otherwise, it asks control. The node runs the read with a time limit. It sends a limited set of rows. If the stream fails, the tenant must treat the answer as incomplete.

documents.title: Litefleet: usage delivery and spill explained
documents.plain: This walkthrough shows the normal path, then the alternative durable path, not two mandatory sends for each event. Completed reads emit an event; a committed execute emits one per statement. Four shippers deliver queued batches with a 2 second HTTP budget. Queue capacity is 1024 and enqueue wait is 20 ms; overflow and failed batches are stored. Every 5 seconds the sweeper reads at most 500 outbox rows, sends batches and deletes each batch only after success. SIGTERM spills pending events and waits up to 3 seconds for in-flight sends, saving stuck batches too. Redelivery can occur; the fake deduplicates by ID in memory. Abrupt process death can lose queued events, and disk write errors are logged, so this is not an exactly-once or crash-lossless guarantee. The independent heartbeat-to-registry ledger is shown in Containers.

ste.text: The node first tries to queue usage in memory. It stores overflow and failed sends in the outbox. A worker sends stored rows again. It deletes rows after success. A normal stop saves pending events. A sudden crash can lose events that are still in memory.

documents.title: Litefleet: Compose lab deployment explained
documents.plain: This is the actual Compose lab, not a production deployment recommendation. Three gateways share HAProxy; two nodes have distinct persistent volumes and cannot substitute for one another. The five Toxiproxy listeners forward gateway/control, gateway/node and node/partner traffic. Control-to-node lifecycle calls and node heartbeats bypass those listeners. Prometheus scrapes each configured target; postgres-exporter queries Postgres. pgdata and blobs persist; Prometheus uses ephemeral tmpfs. The jobs profile supplies a one-shot migrate/backfill/contract command. The maintenance profile runs the purger (enabled by lab/up.sh at this tag); lab tools seed files, apply load and use DuckDB over results and read-only node mounts. The host harness injects faults through Toxiproxy, fake admin modes and Docker, outside application code. Runtime instance nodes refer to the logical containers; volumes and tools are lab infrastructure, not new production services.

ste.text: The lab runs three gateways and two nodes. Each node has its own volume. The proxy adds network faults. Control sends lifecycle commands directly to nodes. Prometheus reads metrics. Optional jobs change the schema and purge old usage. Lab tools create load and read reports.
